completeness.why: copyPreviousMonth and setZero take the whole selection from shouldWriteMonthBudget, setZero picking its hidden-inclusive variation with the explicit 'zero' action; setNMonthAvg takes the sign from averageToBudgetAmount. The three averages call the shared selection (and set3MonthAvg the shared sign), but their own SQL still filters c.hidden = 0 AND g.hidden = 0, so the hidden rule is still decided at each of those sites (twice), which makes them partial.

interface.why: shouldWriteMonthBudget takes the category, an explicit action selector that makes the preserved setZero inconsistency visible, and the tracking-budget flag; averageToBudgetAmount takes only the amount and is_income. The selector names actions ('copy-previous' vs 'average' behave the same) rather than the real variation (include hidden or not), and MonthActionCategory restates BudgetData's fields.

disguised_duplication.where: No logic is reshaped into a disguised copy; the hidden filter left in the three identical average SQL queries in actions.ts is pre-existing duplication that the diff leaves in place rather than disguises.
